title: The characteristic polynomial on a finite locally free module is multiplicative on direct sums
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $M_1,M_2$ $A$-modules and $n_1,n_2\ge0$ such that for $k=1,2$ there are $f^{(k)}_1,\dots,f^{(k)}_{r_k}\in A$ generating the unit ideal with $(M_k)_{f^{(k)}_i}$ free of rank $n_k$ over $A_{f^{(k)}_i}$, and let $\varphi_k:M_k\to M_k$ be $A$-linear. Then $M=M_1\oplus M_2$ is finite locally free of constant rank $n_1+n_2$ (the products $f^{(1)}_if^{(2)}_j$ generate the unit ideal and $M_{f^{(1)}_if^{(2)}_j}$ is free of rank $n_1+n_2$), and $\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_1\oplus\varphi_2:M\to M)=\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_1:M_1\to M_1)\cdot\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_2:M_2\to M_2)$ in $A[T]$ [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free].

proof.text: The products $g_{ij}=f^{(1)}_if^{(2)}_j$ ($1\le i\le r_1$, $1\le j\le r_2$) generate the unit ideal of $A$: choose $a_i,b_j\in A$ with $\sum_ia_if^{(1)}_i=1=\sum_jb_jf^{(2)}_j$; multiplying the two sums gives $\sum_{i,j}a_ib_j\,g_{ij}=1$.

proof.text: Fix $(i,j)$, put $g=g_{ij}$ and $A'=A_g$. For $k=1,2$, $M_k\otimes_AA'$ is a free $A'$-module of rank $n_k$. For $k=1$ put $f=f^{(1)}_i$ (for $k=2$, $f=f^{(2)}_j$; the argument is the same). By hypothesis $(M_1)_f$ is free of rank $n_1$ over $A_f$, so $M_1\otimes_AA_f$ is free of rank $n_1$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-tensor-iso]. The element $f$ divides $g$ and $g$ is invertible in $A_g$, so $f$ is invertible in $A_g$ ($f\cdot(f^{(2)}_j/g)=1$); hence the canonical map $A_f\to A_g$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] (for the module $A$; it is the ring map $a/f^e\mapsto (f^{(2)}_j)^ea/g^e$) is a ring homomorphism under $A$, and [lem-weil-pbc-free-base-change-tower] applied to $A\to A_f\to A_g$ and $M_1$ shows that $M_1\otimes_AA_g$ is free of rank $n_1$ over $A_g$.

proof.text: With $g,A'$ as in step 2 and $M=M_1\oplus M_2$, $\varphi=\varphi_1\oplus\varphi_2$: the map $M\otimes_AA'\to(M_1\otimes_AA')\oplus(M_2\otimes_AA')$, $(x_1,x_2)\otimes b\mapsto(x_1\otimes b,x_2\otimes b)$, is an isomorphism of $A'$-modules (tensor product commutes with finite direct sums; the inverse is $(y_1,y_2)\mapsto\iota_1(y_1)+\iota_2(y_2)$ with $\iota_k\otimes1$ induced by the inclusions), and on generators one checks that it carries $\varphi\otimes1$ to $(\varphi_1\otimes1)\oplus(\varphi_2\otimes1)$. By step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-direct-sum-free] the right side is free of rank $n_1+n_2$, hence so is $M\otimes_AA'$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-tensor-iso] so is $M_g=M_{f^{(1)}_if^{(2)}_j}$. Together with step 1 this proves the first assertion: $M$ is finite locally free of constant rank $n_1+n_2$ on the standard covering by the $g_{ij}$; in particular $\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi:M\to M)$ is defined [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free].

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), proof of (3)$\Rightarrow$(1), the identity CharPol$_A(T:B\to B)$ = CharPol$_A(T:eB\to eB)$ CharPol$_A(T:(1-e)B\to(1-e)B)$ ('Details omitted'); written out by the agent

proof.text: With $g,A'$ as in step 2, let $\rho:A[T]\to A'[T]$ be the map applying $A\to A'$ to the coefficients (a ring homomorphism). By steps 2 and 3, $M_1\otimes_AA'$, $M_2\otimes_AA'$ and $M\otimes_AA'$ are free of ranks $n_1$, $n_2$, $n_1+n_2$, so the characterizing property of [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free] (the polynomial of [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence]) applies to each with the ring map $A\to A'$: $\rho(\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_k))=\det(T-\varphi_k\otimes1)$ on $M_k\otimes_AA'$ and $\rho(\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi))=\det(T-\varphi\otimes1)$ on $M\otimes_AA'$. A characteristic polynomial does not change under an isomorphism of free modules that intertwines the endomorphisms (compute it in a basis and its image), so by step 3 $\det(T-\varphi\otimes1)=\det(T-((\varphi_1\otimes1)\oplus(\varphi_2\otimes1)))$, which is $\det(T-\varphi_1\otimes1)\det(T-\varphi_2\otimes1)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-direct-sum-free] (with $B=A'$, $N_k=M_k\otimes_AA'$, $\psi_k=\varphi_k\otimes1$). Hence $\rho(\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi))=\rho(\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_1))\rho(\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_2))=\rho(\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_1)\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_2))$.

proof.text: Write $\delta=\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi)-\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_1)\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_2)=\sum_mc_mT^m\in A[T]$. By step 4, for every $(i,j)$ each coefficient satisfies $c_m/1=0$ in $A_{g_{ij}}$, the localization of the $A$-module $A$ at $g_{ij}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. The $g_{ij}$ generate the unit ideal (step 1), so [lem-weil-pbc-localized-span-eq-zero] (with $R=A$, $M=A$, $s=\{g_{ij}\}$) gives $c_m=0$ for all $m$. Hence $\delta=0$, i.e. $\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_1\oplus\varphi_2)=\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_1)\cdot\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_2)$.

lean.statement: theorem locallyFreeCharpoly_prodMap {A : Type u} {M₁ : Type v₁} {M₂ : Type v₂} [CommRing A] [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module A M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module A M₂] {n₁ n₂ r₁ r₂ : ℕ} (f₁ : Fin r₁ → A) (f₂ : Fin r₂ → A) (hgen₁ : Ideal.span (Set.range f₁) = ⊤) (hgen₂ : Ideal.span (Set.range f₂) = ⊤) (hfree₁ : ∀ i : Fin r₁, ∃ _e : Module.Basis (Fin n₁) (Localization.Away (f₁ i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f₁ i) M₁), True) (hfree₂ : ∀ j : Fin r₂, ∃ _e : Module.Basis (Fin n₂) (Localization.Away (f₂ j)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f₂ j) M₂), True) (φ₁ : M₁ →ₗ[A] M₁) (φ₂ : M₂ →ₗ[A] M₂) : let g : Fin (r₁ * r₂) → A := fun k ↦ f₁ (finProdFinEquiv.symm k).1 * f₂ (finProdFinEquiv.symm k).2; ∃ (hggen : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤) (hgfree : ∀ k : Fin (r₁ * r₂), ∃ _e : Module.Basis (Fin (n₁ + n₂)) (Localization.Away (g k)) (LocalizedModule.Away (g k) (M₁ × M₂)), True), locallyFreeCharpoly g hggen hgfree (φ₁.prodMap φ₂) = locallyFreeCharpoly f₁ hgen₁ hfree₁ φ₁ * locallyFreeCharpoly f₂ hgen₂ hfree₂ φ₂
